/-!
# Erdős Problem 462

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/462](https://www.erdosproblems.com/462)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos462

open Filter
open scoped BigOperators

/--
Let $p(n)$ denote the least prime factor of $n$. Is there a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\sum_{x\leq n\leq x+C\sqrt{x}(\log x)^2}\frac{p(n)}{n}\gg 1$$
for all sufficiently large $x$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_462 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C c : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      c ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc x
        ⌊(x : ℝ) + C * Real.sqrt x * (Real.log x) ^ 2⌋₊, (n.minFac : ℝ) / n := by
  sorry

end Erdos462

reformulations.difference: The informal condition for all large x is discretized to x : ℕ, with the real upper endpoint replaced by its natural floor.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The floor exactly encodes the closed upper bound for integer summation indices. Allowing real starting points gives an equivalent existence claim: write L(x) = √x(log x)^2 and m = ⌈x⌉. For sufficiently large x, L(m) ≤ 8L(x) and L(x) ≥ 1, so m + C L(m) ≤ x + (1 + 8C)L(x). Thus the interval starting at m is contained in the real-start interval with constant 1 + 8C. All summands are nonnegative, so the same positive lower bound c applies. Conversely, specialize the real-start statement to integer x. The full equivalence was proved without sorry as Review462.nat_real_equivalent in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.
